identity.title: GA-NIFS: High number of dual active galactic nuclei at z ∼ 3

paper_type_evidence.loc: 5.7 Stellar masses of AGN host galaxies
paper_type_evidence.quote: Archival ALMA data (2016.1.00463.S, PI: Y. Matsuda) tracing far-IR emission at $\sim 1$ mm shows that COS1638-B is brighter than the primary AGN host

question.value: What fraction of AGNs at 2<z<6 in the GA-NIFS JWST/NIRSpec IFS sample have dual or multiple AGN companions, and how does it compare with cosmological simulations?

evidence.quote: This study is aimed at providing a first observational estimate of the fraction of dual AGNs at $2 < z < 6$ by analysing a sample of 16 AGNs observed with the JWST Near-InfraRed Spectrograph (NIRSpec) in integral field mode

evidence.loc: 5.7 Stellar masses of AGN host galaxies

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA ~1 mm emission shows COS1638-B is brighter than the primary AGN host, indicating dust at the secondary AGN

evidence.quote: a significant amount of dust is located at the position of the secondary AGN

claims.hypothesis: Dual AGNs are more common at z~3 than expected
claims.experiment: Search of 16 GA-NIFS AGN fields for companions with BPT/UV diagnostics, compared with Horizon-AGN
claims.result: 3-5 multiple AGN systems out of 16 (~20-30%) versus ~10% predicted
claims.finding: Multiple AGNs moderately exceed predictions; sample too small to be conclusive

evidence.quote: our inferred fraction of dual AGN moderately exceeds predictions from cosmological simulations that mimic our observational criteria ($\sim 10$%)

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample size prevents conclusions about simulations underestimating dual AGNs

evidence.quote: precludes us from conclusively determining whether Horizon-AGN cosmological simulations underestimate the number of dual AGNs at high-$z$
